verified_signals.entity: Central Bank of BiH (CBBiH) / IPS BiH
verified_signals.signal: CBBiH went live with the domestic instant payment system (IPS BiH - 'instant payments' means a credit transfer that reaches the payee's account in seconds, any hour of any day) on 20/07/2026. CBBiH calls it the biggest step in modernising BiH payment infrastructure in 25 years. The system is available from day one to all commercial banks; the initial participants are Intesa Sanpaolo Banka BiH, Raiffeisen Bank BiH and Sparkasse Bank BiH, which together hold a quarter of banking-sector assets. Operating hours are 24/7/365. The CBBiH per-transaction fee is lower than the existing giro-clearing fee. The system is a clone of the ECB's TIPS platform, adapted for the Western Balkans by Banca d'Italia with ECB consent; the EU allocated EUR 2 million for the TIPS Clone project and for financing its maintenance in the first year. CBBiH says it will add overlay services, explicitly naming QR code payments, and cross-border payments at a later stage.
verified_signals.source_name: CBBiH press release, 'Centralna banka Bosne i Hercegovine pustila u funkciju domaci sistem instant placanja' (bs)
verified_signals.implies: Every remaining BiH bank must now do an ISO 20022 / 24x7x365 payments-rail integration, real-time fraud/AML screening and always-on liquidity monitoring. Direct pull for Printec transaction monitoring, AML/compliance and HSM/security, plus POS/acquiring tie-ins once the QR overlay arrives at the till. Note the EUR 2m EU envelope funds the CENTRAL platform and its first-year maintenance only - it is not bank-side integration budget, so bank-level spend is additive and unquantified.
verified_signals.followup: Scheme rulebook already obtained and verified (see the IPS BiH rulebook signal). Next: get the CBBiH QR-code specification when published, and map which of the 18 not-yet-connected banks have no real-time transaction monitoring.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Fetched the CBBiH page directly with a desktop User-Agent (WebFetch/plain curl gets HTTP 500 from cbbh.ba; a Chrome UA returns HTTP 200). Every element of the researcher's claim is stated verbatim in the release: date 20.7.2026, the three named initial banks, 'cetvrtinu ukupne aktive bankarskog sektora' (a quarter of total sector assets), fee lower than giro clearing, Banca d'Italia adaptation with ECB consent, European Commission and EU Delegation support. ADDED two verified facts the researcher omitted: the EU contribution is stated twice as EUR 2 million (for the TIPS Clone project and first-year maintenance), and CBBiH names QR code as a planned overlay service with cross-border payments in a later phase. No figure was changed.

verified_signals.entity: BiH SEPA accession / CBBiH and both entity parliaments
verified_signals.signal: On 28/07/2026 the FBiH Parliament's House of Representatives adopted the harmonised set of financial laws, after the RS National Assembly had already done so, which CBBiH says fulfils all regulatory preconditions for BiH to submit its official application to join SEPA (the Single Euro Payments Area, in which cross-border euro payments are executed on the same terms as domestic ones). CBBiH submitted a DRAFT application on 12/12/2025 and says conditions now exist to file the official application with the European Commission and the European Payments Council. CBBiH established and chairs the SEPA Coordination Committee, which includes the entity finance ministries, both banking agencies and the BiH Banking Association. CBBiH notes BiH does over 80% of its foreign trade with SEPA countries and that diaspora remittances of nearly KM 3 billion a year come mostly from SEPA countries. SEPA currently covers all 27 EU member states plus 14 other jurisdictions including the UK, Switzerland, Albania, Serbia, North Macedonia and Montenegro. NO OFFICIAL TIMETABLE: neither this release nor any primary CBBiH source I could reach states an end-2026 membership target.
verified_signals.source_name: CBBiH press release, 'BiH korak blize SEPA-i: Usvojeni kljucni finansijski zakoni u oba entiteta' (bs)
verified_signals.implies: SEPA entry forces IBAN/ISO 20022 migration, SCT and SDD scheme compliance and sanctions/AML screening upgrades across all 22 licensed BiH banks in a compressed window - a country-wide compliance and payments-modernisation programme. Because the enabling laws have now passed in both entities, this has moved from lobbying to execution risk for the banks.
verified_signals.likelihood: High for the application being filed; membership decision timing not officially stated
verified_signals.followup: Obtain the entity payment-services law texts from Sluzbene novine FBiH and Sluzbeni glasnik RS, and press CBBiH for the published SEPA roadmap milestones; identify which of the 22 banks lack ISO 20022 capability. Separately, source the governor's SEPA timing statement to a verbatim transcript before it is used in any customer-facing material.

verified_signals.entity: BiH ATM and POS market (all 22 banks) - CBBiH card-business report
verified_signals.signal: Per CBBiH's annual card-business report, installed ATMs in BiH rose to 1,868 at 31/12/2025 from 1,767 at end-2024, a net gain of 101 machines. The mix shifted sharply: cash-in/cash-out ATMs (machines that both take deposits and dispense, i.e. recycler-capable) rose to 567 from 345 (+222), withdrawal-only ATMs fell to 1,281 from 1,294 (-13), and bill-payment ATMs collapsed to 20 from 128 (-108). POS terminals reached 37,895 (37,647 in merchants, 248 at bank counters) from 35,035. Active cards 2,657,020 (2,585,419 in 2024); 215,077,126 transactions worth KM 21,102,734,732; the cash share of card turnover realised at ATM and POS fell to 65% from 68%. IMPORTANT ARITHMETIC CAVEAT: because the total fleet grew by only 101 while the deposit-capable category grew by 222, roughly half of that +222 is category migration - existing withdrawal-only and bill-payment units being replaced or reclassified - not 222 incremental machines added to the country.
verified_signals.source_name: CBBiH, 'Karticarstvo u BiH u 2025. godini', Payment Systems Department, section 12 'ATM i POS uredaji'
verified_signals.implies: Hard regulator evidence of a recycler-led refresh cycle: the deposit-capable installed base grew 64% in one year while the total fleet grew 6%. Whether the units were incremental or replacements, both are hardware-and-service revenue events, so this remains the clearest cash-automation demand signal in BiH. The bill-payment kiosk category all but disappearing (128 to 20) is consistent with those functions being folded into multifunction ATMs, but CBBiH does not say so - that is inference.
verified_signals.likelihood: Very high - reported by the regulator, trend running since 2021
verified_signals.followup: Ask CBBiH Payment Systems for the per-bank ATM split and 2026 interim data (the published report gives national totals only, no bank or OEM breakdown); cross-check against FBA Tabela 2 and the ABRS equivalent to infer which banks drove the +222.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Downloaded the 20-page PDF (the download endpoint serves application/pdf to a desktop UA) and read the source table on p17 directly. Every figure matches to the unit: 2025 row = 1,281 isplatni / 567 uplatno-isplatni / 20 placanja racuna / 1,868 total ATM / 37,647 POS trgovine / 248 POS gotovina / 37,895 total POS; 2024 row = 1,294 / 345 / 128 / 1,767 / 34,687 / 348 / 35,035. Active cards 2.657.020 and total transaction value 21.102.734.732 KM confirmed; transaction count is 215,077,126 (researcher's '215.1m' is correct rounding); the 65% vs 68% cash share is stated verbatim. NO FIGURE WAS WRONG. I ADDED the arithmetic caveat the researcher missed: net fleet growth was only +101, so the +222 deposit-capable figure is not 222 net-new machines - about half comes from the -13 withdrawal-only and -108 bill-payment categories. This does not reduce the opportunity (replacements are still sales) but the +222 must not be quoted to a customer as 222 new installations. opp_size kept at XL on the footprint-wide test: 22 banks, ~1,900 machines, an active refresh cycle - not because any single named deal of that size exists.

verified_signals.entity: CBBiH IPS BiH scheme rulebook - 'Odluka o pravilima rada sistema instant placanja'
verified_signals.signal: The CBBiH Governing Board decision of 10/07/2026 (7th session) sets binding IPS BiH rules. Art. 13: payment orders must be denominated in BAM; the maximum single transaction is 5,000.00 BAM; the MANDATORY channel for initiating a payment is a mobile or electronic payment platform; a QR code may be used to initiate a payment per a specification CBBiH will publish. Art. 12: maximum end-to-end settlement time is 10 seconds, gross, irrevocable and final. Art. 7 makes participation compulsory: any bank that executed at least 1 million transactions cumulatively across the RTGS (BPRV) and giro-clearing systems between 01/01/2026 and 30/06/2026 must be an IPS BiH participant from 01/01/2027; any bank exceeding 500 thousand cumulative transactions in a calendar year must join from 1 July of the following year. Art. 5: a direct participant must have an established ESMIG connection, a payment-operations licence, a reserve account at CBBiH, an IPS BiH settlement account, a signed statement accepting the rulebook, and must pass CBBiH test scenarios. Indirect participants (non-bank payment service providers) additionally need a contract with a direct-participant bank that provides their liquidity.
verified_signals.source_name: CBBiH, 'Odluka o pravilima rada sistema instant placanja Centralne banke Bosne i Hercegovine' (58-page PDF, scanned)
verified_signals.implies: A dated compliance cliff: the largest BiH banks are legally obliged to be live on IPS BiH by 01/01/2027, and every joiner needs a mobile or e-payment front end (the rulebook makes this the only permitted initiation channel, so any bank without a working mobile app cannot comply), an ESMIG link, QR acceptance, and 10-second processing with fraud controls that must run inside that 10-second window. Directly addressable by Printec digital onboarding/eKYC, transaction monitoring, AML and HSM/security, and by POS/acquiring for QR merchant acceptance. The Art. 7(2) rolling 500k trigger means the mandate keeps catching smaller banks year after year.
verified_signals.likelihood: Certain - binding regulatory decision already in force
verified_signals.followup: Get CBBiH RTGS/giro statistics for H1-2026 to identify which banks cross the 1m-transaction test and are therefore legally obliged to be live by 01/01/2027; screen those for absence of a mobile payment platform today; watch for publication of the CBBiH QR-code specification.
verified_signals.verifier_note: This was the highest-risk claim in the file and it stands up completely. I downloaded the 17 MB scanned PDF and OCR-extracted all 58 pages, then read Articles 5, 7, 12 and 13 in both the Latin and Cyrillic renderings of the text. Verbatim confirmations: '7. sjednici, odrzanoj 10.7.2026'; Art. 7(1) 'minimalno jedan milion transakcija kumulativno u BPRV i zirokliring sistemu, obavezna je da bude ucesnik IPS BiH od 1.1.2027. godine'; Art. 7(2) 'preko 500 hiljada transakcija ... pocevsi od 1.7. naredne godine'; Art. 12 'maksimalnom vremenu za okoncanje transakcije od 10 sekundi, pri cemu je poravnanje neopozivo i konacno'; Art. 13(1) 'obavezno glase na BAM'; Art. 13(2) 'Maksimalni iznos pojedinacne transakcije ... je 5.000,00 BAM'; Art. 13(3) 'Obavezni kanal za iniciranje placanja ... je mobilna ili elektronska platforma za placanje'; Art. 13(4) QR code per a CBBiH-published specification. Art. 5 conditions confirmed and I ADDED two the researcher missed: an open IPS BiH settlement account and a signed rulebook-acceptance statement (Annex 1). Also added the indirect-participant liquidity-contract requirement. No figure changed.

verified_signals.entity: Raiffeisen Bank International / Addiko Bank AG (incl. Addiko Bank dd Sarajevo and Addiko Bank ad Banja Luka)
verified_signals.signal: RBI's contested bid for Addiko Bank AG cleared its acceptance threshold. As of 29/07/2026 17:00 CEST, when the acceptance period expired, RBI had received declarations of acceptance for 10,831,435 Addiko shares, equal to 56.16% of all Addiko shares subject to the offer, exceeding its minimum acceptance threshold of more than 55%. That total includes 1,878,167 shares held by Alta Group d.o.o., equal to 9.63% of all issued Addiko shares. RBI's offer dates from 14/05/2026 under sec. 25a of the Austrian Takeover Act. RBI's threshold had been lowered to more than 55% on 10/07/2026, the rival NLB offer's threshold was lowered to more than 50% on 17/07/2026, and the Austrian Takeover Commission extended both acceptance periods from 22/07/2026 to 29/07/2026. NOT YET SETTLED: RBI states explicitly that this does not yet constitute publication of the official result under sec. 19(2) of the Austrian Takeover Act, that announcement had still not appeared as of 31/07/2026, and regulatory approvals remain outstanding. Whether NLB's competing offer failed its own threshold is NOT confirmed by any primary source - it is a strong inference only, because acceptances are exclusive and RBI holds 56.16% of the shares subject to the offer.
verified_signals.source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International AG ad-hoc announcement distributed via EQS (issuer-authored regulatory disclosure); Addiko Bank AG 'Takeover Offer' page for threshold and deadline changes
verified_signals.implies: If it closes, BiH gets a large in-market bank merger: Raiffeisen Bank dd BiH plus Addiko Bank dd Sarajevo and Addiko Bank ad Banja Luka, spanning both entities. Integration means core and channel migration, branch and ATM fleet rationalisation and re-siting, card portfolio and acquiring consolidation, and a single AML/monitoring stack - classic Printec managed-services, ATM refresh and migration territory. The counterweight is real: RBI Group standardises on incumbent group vendors, so a BiH-local supplier is more likely to win decommissioning, migration and site-services work than the strategic platform.

verified_signals.entity: Bosnia & Herzegovina (FATF grey list) / Banking Agency of FBiH (FBA)
verified_signals.signal: At its plenary of 19/06/2026 the FATF placed Bosnia and Herzegovina on the list of jurisdictions under increased monitoring (the 'grey list' - countries with strategic anti-money-laundering deficiencies that have committed to a time-bound action plan), pointing to needed improvements in preventing money laundering and terrorist financing. The FBA states the banking system was assessed within the MoneyVal evaluation as one of the best-regulated areas in BiH, that the classification is not connected to the stability or quality of the banking system, regulation or supervision under FBA's remit, and that the reasons relate to wider legal and institutional framework questions beyond banking. The FBA nonetheless concedes that, taking account of the MoneyVal findings and the Action Plan measures, the current classification 'may have limited effects on the efficiency of the performance of banking services in international business'. An Action Plan of measures applies.
verified_signals.source_name: Agencija za bankarstvo Federacije BiH (FBA), 'Moneyval: Informacija o procjeni i ogranicenim efektima na bankarski sistem u vezi sa klasifikacijom na sivu listu'
verified_signals.implies: Grey-listing pushes every BiH bank and its correspondent banks into enhanced due diligence, stronger sanctions and PEP screening, better suspicious-transaction-report quality and demonstrable transaction monitoring. It lands in the same quarter as instant payments going live, which compresses the screening window from days to seconds - the two together are the strongest AML/compliance demand trigger in BiH right now. Squarely Printec AML/compliance, transaction monitoring and eKYC territory. Caveat for positioning: the FBA's public line is that the banking system is NOT the problem, so a pitch framed as 'your bank is deficient' will not land; frame it as correspondent-bank and EDD pressure instead.
verified_signals.likelihood: Certain - listing is in force; grey-list exit typically takes years
verified_signals.followup: Obtain the FATF public statement and the BiH Action Plan items with their deadlines (fatf-gafi.org blocks automated access - try a browser session or the MoneyVal site); check which BiH banks have lost or repriced correspondent relationships since 19/06/2026; approach FBA- and ABRS-supervised banks on monitoring-tool upgrades.

verified_signals.entity: Agencija za bankarstvo FBiH (FBA) - 2026 supervisory expectations
verified_signals.signal: The FBA published 'Supervizorska ocekivanja u vezi sa postupanjem banaka u 2026. godini' (document dated February 2026; FBA notice of publication 12/02/2026) setting 11 supervisory priorities. Item 5 ('Preparing for extreme technology and cyber risk scenarios') requires banks to strengthen digital resilience with regular resilience testing including penetration testing and red-team exercises; to improve ICT security controls through multi-layer protection, data encryption, network segmentation and continuous activity monitoring; to ensure early attack-detection systems, automated responses and business continuity and recovery plans, with continuity plans covering scenarios requiring systems to be rebuilt 'from zero'; and to integrate third-party and technology-disruptor risk into risk assessment, with a clear register of every activity outsourced to external partners. Item 9 (AML/CFT) requires transaction-monitoring systems tuned to real BiH client behaviour - explicitly naming cash flows, remittances from abroad, cross-border payments and financing - with improved analytics and automation but clearly defined human assessment and escalation, so that controls are neither excessively formalistic nor blind to real threats; it also requires improved timeliness and quality of suspicious-transaction reports per the National Risk Assessment, and interlinked sanctions/beneficial-owner/end-use controls for proliferation financing. Item 10 requires banks to define payment-services development goals and activities in their business strategies and to prepare for BiH's accession to SEPA.
verified_signals.source_name: FBA, 'Supervizorska ocekivanja u vezi sa postupanjem banaka u 2026. godini' (10-page PDF)
verified_signals.implies: A named regulator shopping list that maps to the Printec catalogue almost line by line: transaction monitoring and AML analytics, HSM/security and encryption, penetration testing, and managed services. Use it as the door-opener with every FBiH bank's CRO and CISO. The important caveat, which is in the same item, is that item 5 also hardens the outsourcing bar: any managed service must come with a documented third-party risk register and board-level oversight, so a Printec managed-services proposal has to arrive with that documentation pack or it becomes a supervisory finding for the client.
verified_signals.likelihood: High - these are the stated priorities for FBA supervisory reviews during 2026
verified_signals.followup: Obtain the ABRS (Republika Srpska) equivalent supervisory expectations for 2026 to cover the other entity, which is still a gap; ask FBiH banks which of the 11 items they are behind on. Note the document is FBiH-only and does not bind the 8 RS-headquartered banks.
verified_signals.verifier_note: I downloaded and text-extracted the 10-page PDF and read items 5, 9 and 10 in full. verified_signals.entity: FBiH banking sector - ATM/POS/branch network (FBA data)
verified_signals.signal: Per FBA's information on the FBiH banking system at 31/12/2025: the ATM network reported in FBA Tabela 2 totalled 1,447 machines against 1,369 a year earlier (+78) and 28,632 POS terminals against 27,412, across 413 branches/higher organisational units (410 a year earlier) and 124 other organisational units (125). Read the composition carefully: 1,385 of those ATMs belong to FBiH-headquartered banks measured ACROSS THE WHOLE OF BiH (1,326 in 2024), and 62 belong to RS-headquartered banks' units inside FBiH (43 in 2024) - so RS banks added 19 ATMs in the Federation in one year while also raising their FBiH branch count from 19 to 23. Individuals' mobile-banking transactions rose to 6,650,858 from 5,581,193 (+19%) worth KM 2.25bn, while individuals' ATM card transactions still rose to 23,595,549 worth KM 6.66bn (from 23,131,263 / KM 6.19bn). Banks filed 528 suspicious transaction reports in 2025 (523 in 2024), and late filings - those made after the 3-day deadline - fell sharply from 293 to 61.
verified_signals.source_name: FBA, 'Informacija o subjektima bankarskog sistema FBiH sa stanjem na dan 31.12.2025' - accompanying tables workbook, Tabele 2, 67, 69, 71
verified_signals.implies: Branch count is essentially flat while ATMs and POS keep growing and mobile use accelerates - the classic 'cash out of the branch, into self-service' pattern that recyclers and ATM managed services are sold into. Note that ATM cash volumes are NOT falling in absolute terms even as mobile grows 19%, which is the argument for deposit automation rather than fleet reduction. RS banks expanding ATMs into the Federation is a live cross-entity land-grab worth chasing (Nova banka, Atos Bank, Addiko RS, NLB RS, MF banka). The STR data is a useful wedge: late filings collapsing from 293 to 61 shows FBiH banks are already investing in AML process, so the sale is upgrade-and-automate, not greenfield.
verified_signals.likelihood: High - regulator data, trend confirmed two years running

verified_signals.verifier_note: I downloaded the workbook and read the four cited sheets cell by cell. ALL FIGURES CONFIRMED EXACTLY. Tabela 2: 2024 totals 410 / 125 / 27,412 / 1,369 and 2025 totals 413 / 124 / 28,632 / 1,447; RS banks' units in FBiH 19 to 23 branches and 43 to 62 ATMs. Tabela 67: individuals' mobile banking 5,581,193 to 6,650,858 transactions and KM 1,636,014k to KM 2,254,686k. Tabela 69: individuals' ATM row 23,131,263 / KM 6,187,855k in 2024 to 23,595,549 / KM 6,656,513k in 2025. Tabela 71: 523 to 528 total STRs, and reports filed after the 3-day deadline 293 to 61. TWO CORRECTIONS. (1) DEFINITION: the researcher wrote 'banks operating in FBiH had 1,447 ATMs'. Tabela 2's first row is labelled 'Banke sa sjedistem u FBiH (na podrucju BiH)' - banks HEADQUARTERED in FBiH counted across the whole of BiH, i.e. including their machines in Republika Srpska. So 1,447 is a hybrid (1,385 FBiH-HQ banks BiH-wide + 62 RS-HQ banks inside FBiH), not a count of machines standing on Federation territory. This matters because it cannot be added to an ABRS RS figure without double-counting. Corrected in the signal text. (2) DATE: the researcher gave 22/04/2026; per the FBA news index the 'Informacija ... 31.12.2025' publication is dated 17.04.2026 (22.04.2026 is the FBA 30th-anniversary item). source_date changed to 17/04/2026. Minor wording: Tabela 69 counts all card transactions at ATMs, not strictly cash withdrawals - restated. Sanity note: FBA's 1,447 and CBBiH's national 1,868 are different populations and must not be subtracted from one another.

(4) NLB published no post-29/07/2026 Addiko item on its 2026 investor-news index, so 'NLB's offer failed' remains inference. NLB's EUR 37/share vs RBI's EUR 26.50 prices appear only in aggregator reporting and were deliberately kept out of the signals. (5) The claim that Governor Selimovic targets SEPA membership by end-2026 was cited by the previous pass with no URL; I found only a secondary summary of a December 2025 interview and dropped the claim. It needs a verbatim transcript before use. (6) cbbh.ba returns HTTP 500 to WebFetch and to plain curl; every CBBiH fetch in this pass required a Chrome desktop User-Agent. The IPS rulebook PDF is a 17 MB scan requiring OCR, so Bosnian diacritics are mangled in extraction - figures were read from both the Latin and Cyrillic renderings to guard against OCR digit errors.
